question: Should universities require standardized test scores?
subject: standardized testing requirements in university admissions
ladder: That runs against the actual outcome data. Follow-up work on the test-optional cohorts found scores predicted first-year performance better than GPA did, and the gap widened at selective institutions.

Grade inflation has destroyed GPA as a comparable signal. The share of applicants reporting an A average has climbed steadily while measured achievement stayed flat — a test is the only cross-school common scale left.
MIT reinstated the requirement, and their stated reason was that dropping it was hurting low-income applicants: without a score, a strong student from an unknown high school had no way to stand out.
Dartmouth, Yale, Brown and Caltech all reversed within the same window, each citing their own internal admissions research. Four independent institutions, four internal reviews, same conclusion.

When scores are removed, weight shifts to essays, recommendations, and extracurriculars — every one of which is more purchasable than test prep. Removing the test made admissions more dependent on family resources, not less.
